doc.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010

title: Rock, bluegrass and pop influences
summary: She listens to rock and pop, grew up on Joni Mitchell and bluegrass with a banjo-playing father, and admires Maura O'Connell.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Who in the classic rock world have you listened to that you may have liked?

I have not just listened to jazz in my life. So much other music. You know in the car we’re more likely to be listening to like Zeppelin, or Jimi Hendrix, or The Beatles or Stevie Wonder or something like that. I grew up on Joni Mitchell and my father is a banjo player. I heard a lot of bluegrass growing up. And you know, for a hot second I considered singing that kind of music. One of my favorite singers on the planet is Maura O’Connell who is a brilliant singer from that genre, a beautiful folk/bluegrass singer. You know I worked a lot with Béla Fleck and Mark O’Connor and her early albums which I just loved. And she was a big influence on me as a singer. You know, so there were so many other influences, and a lot of rock music, I mean a lot. I still love it. I mean and I love pop music.

I have so much fun with today’s pop music. Because it’s a release. Like I’ll go to the gym with like Lady Gaga screaming in my headphones, and it makes the treadmill fun. There is something to be said for every single genre of music. And people who say, “Oh well I just hate this kind of music and won’t listen to it.” Well then try again, because there’s something great about everything.
